summary: This note describes Friant Dam, a concrete gravity dam on the San Joaquin River in central California, straddling the Fresno and Madera County boundary. It was built from 1937 to 1942 by the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation to supply irrigation water to the southern San Joaquin Valley. The dam impounds Millerton Lake, a reservoir north of Fresno.
one_line: Friant Dam is a 1937–1942 concrete gravity dam on California's San Joaquin River that impounds Millerton Lake for irrigation.
key_facts: Friant Dam is a concrete gravity dam on the San Joaquin River in central California, United States.
Friant Dam lies on the boundary of Fresno County and Madera County.
Friant Dam was built between 1937 and 1942.
Friant Dam was built as part of a U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (USBR) water project.
The purpose of the Friant Dam water project was to provide irrigation water to the southern San Joaquin Valley.
Millerton Lake is a reservoir located about north of Fresno (distance not stated in the note).
